rendered: The document does not report any test of the D-HGNR-based probe on the clinical sepsis serum samples. The serum work was done with the L-HGNR probe. The sepsis serum result is for BA@L-HGNRs: the probe guished two types of clinical sepsis serum samples[1] (the start of that sentence reads "Furthermore, BA@L-HGNRs successfully distin-"). In the serum analysis, the groups (septic patients with E. coli, septic patients with E. faecium, and healthy volunteers) gave well-resolved, non-overlapping[2] LDA clusters, which the authors describe as clusters for the three tested serum groups[3], shown in Fig. 5[4]. The authors state the result as potential for accurate bacterial discrimination[5] in serum samples from septic patients[6]. The D-HGNR probe appears only in the aqueous-solution validation, where The BA@D-HGNRs probe with the[7] opposite spatial configuration also effectively validates this phenomenon[8] (Fig. S16). So the document gives no D-HGNR performance results for sepsis serum.
